questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of cases and what they held on government formation:
Case : Holding
1. S.R. Bommai v. Union of India : The floor of the House is the place to test whether a government enjoys majority support
2. Nabam Rebia v. Deputy Speaker : The Governor's discretion under Article 163 is limited, and he cannot summon or advance an Assembly session on his own without ministerial advice
3. Rameshwar Prasad v. Union of India : A Governor may bypass the Assembly and judge a party's majority by letters of support
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Bommai held that majority must be tested in the House and not by the Governor's own assessment, and that minority governments are allowed if they hold the House's confidence. In Nabam Rebia, the Constitution Bench held that Governor's discretion under Article 163 is confined to cases the Constitution expressly marks out, so summoning or advancing a session needs the advice of the ministry. Pair 3 is wrong: Rameshwar Prasad said the Governor cannot bypass the Assembly in determining majority, and cannot leave the State in limbo; he must appoint a government or dissolve.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 21-22; Nabam Rebia (2016) is static

questions.q:
With reference to the Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0, consider the following statements:
1. It is prepared by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and is built on the localisation of Sustainable Development Goals.
2. In its latest results a large number of Gram Panchayats were graded as 'Achievers'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the index covers more than 2.6 lakh panchayats across nine themes drawn from the seventeen goals, and requires Gram Sabha validation of data. Statement 2 is wrong: none reached the top 'Achiever' grade of 90 or above. Only a small share were Front Runners, about 1.4 per cent, with Tripura leading, and nearly half were Aspirants, so the index is used to guide local planning.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 9-10; Article 243G is static

questions.q: The Logistics Ease Across Different States (LEADS) report is released by
o: the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
questions.e: LEADS has been brought out since 2018 by the commerce ministry's industry promotion department, on the lines of the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index, which ranks countries, not States. The 2025 edition moved to four performance tiers. It is separate from NITI Aayog indices, which rank States on other themes. India's logistics cost is put at about 8 per cent of GDP, and the National Logistics Policy and PM GatiShakti aim to lower it.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not correct about the power of the Supreme Court under Article 142?
o: It has been called a power of a different level and quality that ordinary statutes cannot restrict.
The Court has said it must be used with extraordinary care and caution.
It sits within the Constitution's chapter on the Union Judiciary, which covers Articles 124 to 147.
It lets the Court override any provision of the Constitution if it thinks the result is fair.
questions.e: The Court has repeatedly said the power cannot be used to defy express statutory or constitutional provisions; it fills gaps and does substantive justice where the law is silent or falls short. Delhi Judicial Service Association (1991) described its unusual character, and Hitesh Bhatnagar (2011) urged caution. Critics worry about separation of powers, which is why restraint is stressed, while supporters point to legislative vacuum or administrative inaction.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the history of school meals in India, from the earliest to the latest:
1. Renaming as Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman
2. National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education
3. Mid-Day Meal Scheme
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The national programme of nutritional support started in 1995 with dry rations for primary children. In 2004 it became a cooked Mid-Day Meal Scheme, after Supreme Court orders on the right to food. In 2021 it was renamed PM POSHAN and extended to pre-primary classes. The sequence shows a shift from grain to cooked food to a wider nutrition scheme.

questions.q: In a hung Assembly, the order of preference commonly recommended for a Governor inviting a claimant is
o: the single largest party, then a pre-poll alliance, then a post-poll coalition, then President's Rule
a post-poll coalition, then the single largest party, then a pre-poll alliance, then dissolution
the party led by the incumbent Chief Minister, then the single largest party, then a pre-poll alliance

a pre-poll alliance with a majority, then the single largest party with outside support, then a post-poll coalition of all partners, then a post-poll alliance with some partners joining and others supporting
questions.e: Two commissions on Centre-State relations suggested this ladder, the Sarkaria and Punchhi Commissions. A pre-poll alliance gets first claim because voters chose it as a bloc. The single largest party comes next only if it can show outside support. President's Rule under Article 356 is a last resort, not a rung on the ladder. Past departures from this order, as in Goa, Manipur and Karnataka, have drawn criticism.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The power under Article 142 is available to the Supreme Court and not to the High Courts under Article 226.
Statement-II: In Delhi Judicial Service Association v. State of Gujarat (1991), the Supreme Court described the power under Article 142 as one of a different level and quality, which ordinary statutes cannot restrict.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct but the second does not explain the first. The Article, by its terms, belongs to the Supreme Court, and the Court has said that High Courts do not have the same power, though they give relief under their own writ jurisdiction. Statement-II records how the Court has described the breadth of the power, which is a separate point and says nothing about who holds it. The reason High Courts lack it is that the Constitution has not conferred it on them.

questions.q:
Consider the following reports:
1. Crime in India
2. Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India
3. Prison Statistics India
4. Periodic Labour Force Survey
How many of the above are published by the National Crime Records Bureau?
questions.e: Only the first three are correct. They are separate annual reports of the Bureau, which functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs and publishes crime, accidental death and suicide, and prison data. Statement 4 is wrong: the Periodic Labour Force Survey is run by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, which is why it is easily mixed up with other official surveys. The prison data for 2024 showed occupancy easing from the previous year.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 98-100; Vision IAS pp. 15-16; PLFS's publisher is static
questions.it: Reports of NCRB and census bodies

questions.q: NIPUN Bharat, the national mission on foundational literacy and numeracy, is run
o: under PM POSHAN, by the Ministry of Education
under the Integrated Child Development Services, by the Ministry of Women and Child Development
under the National Health Mission, by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
under Samagra Shiksha, by the Ministry of Education
questions.e: The mission aims at children reading with understanding and doing basic arithmetic by Grade 3, and it is launched through Samagra Shiksha, the umbrella school programme. PM POSHAN is the school meal scheme. Early childhood care through anganwadis is under the women and child development ministry, but the foundational learning mission sits with the education ministry, which also supports the national assessment centre PARAKH under the same scheme.

questions.q:
With reference to PM POSHAN, consider the following statements:
1. It is administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development along with the Integrated Child Development Services.
2. Hot cooked meals are provided to children in Balvatika classes as well as Classes I to VIII.
3. A social audit is mandatory in all districts.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The meal is available to pre-primary Balvatika children and to elementary classes in government and aided schools, with community meals on special days under Tithi Bhojan and a social audit required. Statement 1 is wrong: the scheme belongs to the Ministry of Education. Anganwadi Services and the adolescent girls' scheme are the women and child development ministry's, which is a common confusion.

questions.q:
With reference to the administration of Samagra Shiksha, extended in 2026 pending approval for the next Finance Commission cycle, consider the following statements:
1. Its Governing Council is headed by the Minister of Education.
2. Its Project Approval Board is headed by the Minister of Education.
3. It is run by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
4. At the State level it is implemented through a State Implementation Society.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. The Governing Council is headed by the Minister of Education, and the States implement the scheme through a State Implementation Society. Statement 2 is wrong: the Project Approval Board, which clears State plans, is headed by the Secretary of the Department of School Education and Literacy, an official and not the Minister. Statement 3 is wrong: it is a centrally sponsored scheme of the Ministry of Education; the Ministry of Women and Child Development runs anganwadi-based programmes, which is a common confusion.

questions.q:
With reference to the Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram, for which new guidelines were issued in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The 2026 version extends beyond defects, diseases, deficiencies and developmental delays to cover mental-health conditions, behavioural concerns and risk factors for non-communicable diseases.
2. It is implemented through the Integrated Child Development Services Mission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: RBSK 2.0 goes beyond the original four Ds to cover mental-health conditions, behavioural concerns and risk factors such as diabetes and hypertension, and it lists 38 common health conditions. Statement 2 is wrong: the programme was launched in 2013 by the health ministry and runs under the National Health Mission, though screening happens at delivery points, anganwadis and schools, so convergence with other departments is built in.

questions.q:
In the Supreme Court's suo motu case on the Phalodi road accident, consider the following statements:
1. The Court treated safe travel on National Highways as part of the right to life under Article 21.
2. The Court said that safe and well-maintained roads are only a policy goal and not a constitutional obligation.
3. The proceedings were begun on a petition filed by the National Highways Authority of India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. After two accidents with many deaths, the Court acted on its own motion and held that the right to safe travel on highways flows from Article 21, making safe, maintained roads a constitutional obligation and not merely a policy aim. Statement 2 states the opposite. Statement 3 is wrong because the authority was a respondent; the Court itself initiated the case.

questions.q:
Under the screening platforms of RBSK 2.0, consider the following pairs:
Platform : Age group screened
1. Delivery points : Newborns, from birth to six weeks
2. Anganwadi centres : Children from six weeks to six years
3. Government and aided schools : Children from six to eighteen years
4. District Early Intervention Centres : Adolescents above fifteen years only
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct; screening follows the child from birth through pre-school to school. Pair 4 is wrong. The district centres are not a screening platform for one age group. They are referral facilities where children flagged at screening get diagnosis and therapy under one roof, with hub-and-spoke links to secondary and tertiary hospitals, including surgery and cochlear implants.

questions.q:
With reference to Samagra Shiksha, which was extended in 2026 pending approval for the next Finance Commission cycle, consider the following pairs:
Category : Centre-State funding share
1. North-Eastern and Himalayan States : 90:10
2. Other States : 60:40
3. Union Territories without a legislature : 100 per cent central
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. The scheme is centrally sponsored, so States share the cost, but the burden is lighter for hill and North-Eastern States, which get a 90:10 split, and Union Territories without legislatures are fully funded by the Centre. Other States share 60:40. The scheme, run by the Ministry of Education since 2018, merged the earlier Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan and the teacher education scheme.

questions.q:
With reference to the World Migration Report 2026, consider the following pairs:
Statement : Finding
1. Share of international migrants in world population : Higher than in 1990
2. Largest migration corridor in the world : India to the United Arab Emirates
3. Remittances to low- and middle-income countries : About 685 billion dollars in 2024
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. Migrants form about 3.7 per cent of the world's people, up from 2.9 per cent in 1990, and remittances to poorer countries were about 685 billion dollars. Pair 2 is wrong: the largest corridor is Mexico to the United States, and the India-UAE corridor ranks fifth, with India-US sixth. Over three million Indians live in each of these two countries.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Report)
A. World Migration Report
B. Developments and Trends in Multilateral Peace Operations
C. Global Report on Food Crises
D. Global Hepatitis Report
List-II (Publisher)
1. SIPRI
2. International Organization for Migration
3. World Health Organization
4. Global Network Against Food Crises
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The migration report is the International Organization for Migration's, and the 2026 edition counted about 304 million international migrants. The factsheet on peace operations comes from the Stockholm institute, which also publishes the military expenditure data. The food crises report is the product of the network founded in 2016 by the FAO, the EU and the WFP. The hepatitis report is the World Health Organization's. Because all four deal with global problems, they are easily swapped.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 33-35; Vision IAS p. 115

questions.q:
With reference to government formation after the Tamil Nadu election of 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 164(1) the Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor.
2. Under Article 163(2), the Governor's decision on whether a matter is one for his discretion is final.
3. Article 174(2)(b) empowers the Governor to dissolve the Legislative Assembly.
4. The Constitution fixes the number of days a Governor may take to explore possibilities.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Governor appoints the Chief Minister, and the other ministers on that person's advice. Article 163(2) says that the Governor's decision on whether a matter calls for his discretion is final, though courts still examine whether the exercise of the power was arbitrary or mala fide. The Governor may dissolve the Assembly. Statement 4 is wrong: the Constitution speaks of no time limit, so the law says only that he must act within a reasonable time.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 21-22; Articles are static
